reason: Under the Standard-IA minimum object charge question the quote states a 128KB minimum object storage charge and that smaller objects are charged as if 128KB.
The quote states data deleted from S3 Standard-IA within 30 days is charged for a full 30 days.
The quote states Standard-IA offers the durability, throughput and low latency of S3 Standard with a low per-GB storage price and per-GB retrieval charge.
The quote lists Lifecycle tiering from Standard-IA to One Zone-IA, Glacier Instant Retrieval, Glacier Flexible Retrieval and Glacier Deep Archive.
The quote gives both access-frequency rules verbatim: S3 Standard more than once a month, Standard-IA retained at least a month and accessed once every month or two.
The quote states each class charges to store and to access data and to choose by access patterns and retention time for lowest lifetime cost.
The quote states the total volume of data and number of objects you can store in Amazon S3 are unlimited.
The quote states Transfer Acceleration leverages CloudFront's edge locations and routes arriving data to the bucket over an optimized network path.
The quote states Transfer Acceleration supports all bucket level features including multipart uploads.
The quote states that if acceleration is not likely to be faster than a regular transfer, AWS does not charge for it on that transfer and may bypass the system.
The quote states Direct Connect fits a private networking requirement and Transfer Acceleration is best for distributed clients over the public internet or variable network conditions.
The quote says Transfer Acceleration can help accelerate long-distance transfers of larger objects to and from a single bucket; the claim drops the 'larger objects' qualifier.
The quote states a table bucket is purpose-built for storing tables using the Apache Iceberg format.
The quote supports archiving 'your new virtual tapes' directly to Flexible Retrieval and Deep Archive; the claim drops 'new' and so says more than the quote.
Context states S3 is designed to handle traffic for any internet application; the quote states its scale spreads load so no individual application is affected by spikes.
The quote describes two-way replication as a rule from source to replica bucket plus a second rule back, with buckets in the same or different Regions.
Context states a vector bucket is purpose-built for storing and querying vectors; the quote states it uses dedicated vector APIs, not the S3 object APIs.
The quote gives the example rule archiving previous versions to Glacier Flexible Retrieval and deleting after 100 days for a 100-day rollback window.
The FAQ answers yes under its heading, and the quote states only requests to endpoint-specific names use the interface endpoint while others keep using the gateway endpoint.
The quote recommends interface endpoints for on-premises or other-Region VPC access and gateway endpoints for same-Region VPCs as they are not billed.
The quote names the two types, gateway endpoints specified in the route table and interface endpoints using private IPs from the VPC, on-premises or another Region.
The two quotes state S3 Files is built using Amazon EFS and that authoritative data always remains in S3 with two-way background synchronization.
The three quotes under the same FAQ question give the S3 Files, EFS and FSx positioning as the claim states.
The quote states the data model is flat, there is no hierarchy of subbuckets or subfolders, and logical hierarchy is inferred from key name prefixes and delimiters.
Under the Flexible Retrieval heading the quote states objects larger than 5 TB typically finish within 48 hours with up to 300 MBps for any retrieval option.

The quotes state general purpose buckets are the original type, recommended for most use cases, hold any number of objects in all classes except Express One Zone, and store redundantly across multiple AZs.
The Glacier quotas table row gives 40,000 Gigabytes as the maximum size of an archive, not adjustable.

The quotes state the vault-based service no longer accepts new customers, existing data stays accessible indefinitely, AWS recommends the S3 Glacier storage classes, and the maintenance list shows S3 Glacier Direct on October 7, 2025.
The table row gives 'Each supported Region: 2' per account; the claim and scope say per account only and drop the per-Region scope.
The quotas table row gives 35 random restore requests per PiB stored per day.
The quote and its context state locking takes two steps and that in the in-progress state you have 24 hours to validate and must complete the lock before the lock ID expires.
The quotes state Vault Lock enforces controls such as WORM with a Vault Lock policy and that a locked policy can no longer be changed or deleted.
The quotes contrast the two policies: both govern access, the Vault Lock policy can be locked against changes for compliance, the access policy is for controls subject to frequent modification.
The quotas table row gives 1,000 vaults per account in each supported Region, not adjustable.
The quote states the name is unavailable to anyone else in the partition while the bucket exists and becomes available again for anyone when deleted.
The quote states GuardDuty S3 protection analyzes CloudTrail management and data events for S3 resources and monitors them for malicious and suspicious activity.
The quotes state sustained rates typically over 5,000 requests per second to a small number of objects might get HTTP 503 slowdown, and each AWS SDK retries with exponential backoff.
Context says both IA classes are for long-lived infrequently accessed data; the quote states millisecond access similar to S3 Standard and a retrieval fee.
The quote states both IA classes suit objects larger than 128 KB stored at least 30 days and that an object under 128 KB is charged as 128 KB.
The quote states the 30-day minimum and the normal storage charge plus a pro-rated charge for the remainder when deleted, overwritten or transitioned earlier.
